messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert fired: PROD-DNS-LB-HEALTH (P2) — https://pd.example/INC12345 — auto-page to on-call. runbook: https://runbooks/internal/dns-lb-tls\nPagerDuty: Alert details -> service: prod-edge-lb, symptom: TLS handshake failures reported by edge (partial), metric: 5xx spike, source: health-checker/us-west-2. Escalation schedule active.
Samir: ack — I'm on it, pulling logs + checking target groups in us-west-2.
IncidentBot: Samir acknowledged the alert.
Samir: quick findings: target-group arn:tg-0a1b2c has 5/12 targets UNHEALTHY. Health check failures are TLS handshake errors (proxy logs show 'tls: unsupported protocol' and 'tls: unknown alpn' intermittently).
Maria: any visible customer errors? is this impacting traffic broadly or a small subset? :rotating_light:
Owen: Grafana shows a brief spike in 525/526s starting 2026-03-15T14:22Z. Approx 0.6% of requests from prod-frontend. 95th latency increased a bit.
Samir: repro locally -> curl against LB from us-west: ```curl -v https://edge-west.example/health -H 'Host: prod.example.com'```
Samir: sample output: ```* Connected to edge-west (10.0.0.12) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS handshake failed\n* error:1408F10B:SSL routines:SSL3_GET_RECORD:wrong version number\n```
Linus: Did we do a cert rotation or config push earlier? I see cert-rotation job completed ~2h ago across regions.
Maria: Could be cert+ALPN/cipher negotiation combo. But the error looks like a mismatch in TLS protocol or ALPN. Are these backends on an older openssl/libressl?
Samir: digging — 5 of the unhealthy hosts are running an older image (image: prod-backend:v2026-03-13-old) that didn't get the latest distro packages. openssl version on those is 1.0.2.
Owen: If that's the case, some clients (and our proxy) may negotiate ALPN/cipher suites new enough that old openssl fails the handshake.
Samir: mitigation plan: shift traffic away from us-west to eu region temporarily, take unhealthy targets OOS and redeploy with image bump to v2026-03-15 which has openssl 1.1.1.
Maria: good. Also notify Support and drop a short customer-facing blurb if impact grows.
Samir: executing traffic shift (Route53 weighted policy). Command I'll run: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://shift-weight.json``` — applying now.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty escalation timer set — will escalate to team lead if unresolved in 5m.
Samir: weight change applied: eu weight -> 100, us-west -> 0 (temporary). Verifying from curl in eu -> 200 OK.
Owen: Confirming metrics: error rate in prod-frontend dropped ~80% within 30s after weight shift.
Maria: CS notified: "We detected a brief TLS handshake error affecting a small subset of requests in us-west; traffic has been shifted while we remediate. We'll update if anything changes."
Samir: draining unhealthy targets now: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg-0a1b2c --targets Id=i-0abc,Id=i-0def```
Linus: I'll monitor DNS TTL propagation — weight shift is immediate for Route53 but some client caches may still hit us-west for old records up to TTL. Current TTL is 60s.
Owen: PagerDuty: manual acknowledgement of escalation completed.
Samir: redeploying fixed image to the drained instances; new image has openssl 1.1.1 and updated TLS config. Rolling deploy: canary -> remainder. Starting now.
Samir: health checks returning PASS on previously unhealthy hosts after redeploy. Running additional validation for 10m.
Maria: support update: CS updated customers and closed urgent ticket queue. Impact estimated: ~0.7% of requests in us-west had transient TLS errors for ~6 minutes. No data loss.
Owen: Metrics stable, error rate returned to baseline. Shifting weights back to original gradually.
Samir: restored original weights over 3 steps: 25% -> 50% -> 100% across 5 minutes. Verified 200 OK from us-west.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 resolved by Samir at 2026-03-15T14:35Z.
Samir: follow-ups: 1) enforce openssl preflight in deploy CI so nodes with older libs don't get promoted; 2) add runbook step to check ALPN/cipher compatibility after cert rotations; 3) create postmortem PR.
Maria: filing postmortem now: https://redwood/postmortems/INC12345 — assigning to Samir + Linus.
Samir: thanks all, closing thread. :thumbsup:
Owen: nice fast mitigation. Recommend we add a monitoring alert for mismatched TLS version counts per target group.
Linus: noted — will add a metric and an alert.
IncidentBot: Thread closed.
